_comment: Copy this to mcp_servers.json (gitignored) to give the FREE experimenter one or more MCP connectors. Each entry is the SDK's McpServerConfig — stdio {type,command,args,env} or http/sse {type,url,headers} — plus this project's two optional `_`-prefixed keys, which are stripped before the map reaches the SDK. Entries whose NAME starts with '_' are comments and are ignored. Each configured server's tools are permitted to the free agent as mcp__<name>; the capability guard still vets every call, so a connector can never reach memory/, runs/, or credentials. Remove this file (or leave only mcp_servers.example.json) to run with no connectors — the default, byte-identical path. PATHS MUST BE ABSOLUTE: a connector is launched both by the agent, whose cwd is its per-run workspace, and by the deterministic verifier, which may run from anywhere.
_comment_verifiable: `_verifiable: true` is the ONE thing that lets a connector's answer become a KEPT number rather than an unverified caveat (docs/memo_connector_bridge.md, R-MCP-2). It is your assertion, as the operator, that this server is a DETERMINISTIC DATA SOURCE with no language model inside it — because a kept number is re-run through tools/run_mcp_tool.py at verification time, and verification purity forbids a model in that path. Leave it off for anything model-backed or agentic: the agent can still call the connector freely while it explores, and whatever it learns is reported as an honest unverified caveat.

pubchem._description: PubChem compound lookup — resolve a name/CID/SMILES to a structure (compound_identity) or read one curated/computed property (compound_property: MolecularWeight, TPSA, XLogP, HBondDonorCount, ...)

_example_third_party_stdio._description: a third-party server works exactly the same way; ${VAR} is resolved from the environment (keep keys in .env, never here). No _verifiable key: reachable for exploration, cannot back a kept number.
